title: SGS Weekly Recap Top 5
tagline: The week in power: where the world leaned, and why.
discovery_note: Overall, the week leaned Slightly Globalist.

stories.headline: Serbia's students take parliament
stories.summary: Serbia's new parliament met, and the Student List holds a clear majority. Lawmakers elected their pick, university lecturer Aleksandar Chupich, as speaker.
stories.label: Slightly Sovereign
stories.why: Voters turned a street movement into a parliamentary majority.
stories.what_it_means: A street movement now runs the parliament, and a government still has to be formed.
stories.economic_impact: A government still has to be formed.
stories.everyday_example: It's like neighbors outvoting the longtime manager.

stories.headline: Pax Silica protests and arrests in the Philippines
stories.summary: About three hundred protesters were arrested at the US-led Pax Silica hub in the Philippines as Trump arrived. Indigenous families in Tarlac say the new zone will push them off their land. Most were later released, but the project was not stopped.
stories.label: Strongly Globalist
stories.why: A foreign-led bloc project went ahead over local land after mass arrests.
stories.what_it_means: A foreign-led factory zone is going ahead over local land.
stories.economic_impact: Families there stand to lose land.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a chain building on the family farm.

stories.headline: Russian missiles enter Poland; NATO help requested
stories.summary: During a huge Russian strike on Ukraine, three Russian objects came down in southeastern Poland. No one was hurt. Poland called it a provocation and asked NATO for more air defense.
stories.label: Moderately Globalist
stories.why: The war spilled across a NATO border, and Poland asked for more alliance forces.
stories.what_it_means: The war spilled across a NATO border, and Poland wants more help to guard its own skies.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a fight next door throwing bricks over your fence.

stories.headline: Houthis hit Riyadh's wealth-fund tower
stories.summary: In Riyadh, a Houthi attack damaged the tower of Saudi Arabia's wealth fund. Windows were blown out, and no one was hurt. Two days later, more missiles aimed at the capital were intercepted.
stories.label: Strongly Globalist
stories.why: An Iran-backed proxy put a capital's financial tower under fire, then fired again.
stories.what_it_means: This proxy fight is hitting the building that holds the kingdom's money.
stories.everyday_example: It's like smashing the windows of the town bank, then coming back two days later.

stories.headline: Shenzhen peace declaration skips the wars
stories.summary: In Shenzhen, Trump, Xi and Putin issued a four-point declaration toward peace. It covers UN reform, fuel supplies, official immunity, and nuclear risk. It does not mention the wars in Ukraine or Iran.
stories.label: Slightly Globalist
stories.why: Three powers signed a peace declaration that leaves the wars off the page.
stories.what_it_means: They signed a peace label that leaves the wars off the page, and more fuel is only a plan.
stories.economic_impact: More fuel is only a plan.
stories.everyday_example: It's like three neighbors signing a good-fences note while the house next door is still on fire.
